top_signals.title: Domino's Drops on Sales Growth Miss; Bumble Goes Private | Stock Movers
top_signals.summary:
On this episode of Stock Movers:

- Domino's Pizza (DPZ) shares are lower after the restaurant chain reported total domestic stores comp sales growth for the third quarter that missed the average analyst estimate.
- Johnson & Johnson (JNJ) shares are moving as the company reports earnings. J&J raised its profit guidance as demand for newer drugs in cancer and autoimmune diseases overshadowed more anemic growth in the company’s medical device business.
- Bumble (BMBL) shares are halted on news Ithaca is taking Bumble private for $1.3 billion, with a deal price of $6.05 per share. Bumble founder Whitney Wolfe Herd said she would “remain actively involved with Bumble” after the deal, which marks a significant change for the company that was valued at $14 billion when it went public. (Source: Bloomberg)

top_signals.title: New Mountain Bets on Defensive Growth
top_signals.summary: As investors reassess private credit, New Mountain Capital’s Laura Holson says direct lending is offering attractive opportunities with wider spreads and improved lender protections. She joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain why higher rates can benefit floating-rate investments, what risks borrowers face, and why her firm favors defensive-growth sectors such as industrial automation and animal health. (Source: Bloomberg)
